etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French unifier, from Late Latin unificare.

definitions.definition: (transitive) Cause to become one; make into a unit; consolidate; merge; combine.

quote.citation: 2008, Eliza Mada Dalian, In Search of the Miraculous: Healing Into Consciousness‎[1], Expanding Universe Publishing, →ISBN, page 91:
quote.text: Ultimately, all frequencies unify into an unmoving state of zero frequency or vacuum. In other words, all seven sound vibrations or notes unify into silence; all thought frequencies (positive and negative) unify into no-thought  or no-mind; and all seven colors of the rainbow unify into pure space that appears dark when it is invisible and as light when it is visible.
